classification.difficultyReason: Construct an enlargement from an external centre and verify corresponding lengths and angles using instruments.

content.prompt: The following diagram shows an isosceles triangle $ABC$ and a point $O$. Copy or trace the diagram into your exercise book, leaving plenty of room to the right and below your diagram.

spec.description: Upright narrow isosceles triangle with horizontal base BC; O lies well to the left of A at approximately its height. Source blue outlines and red point are ordinary marks rendered black under house style. Coordinates reconstruct proportions without supplying numerical measurements.
spec.mathematics: AB = AC. O is external to the triangle and determines the enlargement rays. No numerical lengths, angles or equality marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The original triangle and centre are permanent givens; the enlarged triangle is absent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use ruler and compasses to apply an enlargement transformation with centre $O$ and enlargement factor $3$. Label your image $A'B'C'$.

answer.short: Triangle $A'B'C'$ with $A'$, $B'$ and $C'$ on rays $OA$, $OB$ and $OC$, respectively, and $OA'=3OA$, $OB'=3OB$, $OC'=3OC$.
answer.worked: Draw rays from $O$ through $A$, $B$ and $C$. Set the compasses to $OA$ and step this distance three times along ray $OA$, starting at $O$, to locate $A'$. Repeat with compass widths $OB$ and $OC$ on the corresponding rays to locate $B'$ and $C'$. Join $A'B'$, $B'C'$ and $C'A'$.

spec.description: Complete enlargement using the same original geometry, with corresponding image coordinates multiplied by three about O. Dashed construction guides distinguish rays from triangle sides.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Verify that each side length of $\triangle A'B'C'$ is three times the matching side length of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.worked:
Measure all three pairs of corresponding sides with a ruler. The measurements should give
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{A'B'}{AB}&=3\\\frac{B'C'}{BC}&=3\\\frac{A'C'}{AC}&=3.\end{aligned}$$
Small differences may arise from construction and measurement accuracy.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use a protractor to verify that each angle of $\triangle A'B'C'$ is equal to the matching angle of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.short: $\angle B'A'C'=\angle BAC$, $\angle A'B'C'=\angle ABC$ and $\angle A'C'B'=\angle ACB$, within measurement accuracy.
answer.worked:
Place the protractor centre at each vertex, align its baseline with one side and measure to the other side. Compare the corresponding measurements:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle B'A'C'&=\angle BAC\\\angle A'B'C'&=\angle ABC\\\angle A'C'B'&=\angle ACB.\end{aligned}$$
Each corresponding pair should agree within measurement accuracy.
